lead.headline: Kauaʻi state offices, most schools, college and courts to reopen Monday
lead.summary: State offices, most public schools, Kauaʻi Community College and Judiciary facilities will reopen September 14 as recovery conditions improve; Kīlauea and Hanalei elementary schools remain closed.
lead.why_it_matters: Families, students and workers need school-specific guidance because most operations are resuming while two campuses still lack power or potable water.
lead.source_name: Office of the Governor, State of Hawaiʻi
body: Kauaʻi state offices, most Hawaiʻi Department of Education public schools, Kauaʻi Community College and state Judiciary facilities are scheduled to reopen Monday, September 14, as the island continues recovering from Hurricane Lowell, according to the Office of the Governor.

Most public schools will return to regular operations after a week of storm-related closures. The state said electricity had been restored to 13 of Kauaʻi’s 15 public school campuses as of Friday afternoon.

Kīlauea Elementary and Hanalei Elementary will remain closed to students and staff Monday because the campuses do not yet have both power and potable water. Chiefess Kamakahelei Middle School will hold its previously scheduled staff professional-development waiver day, with students expected back Tuesday, September 15.

State employees should report to their normal worksites or follow their departments’ regular telework schedules unless supervisors provide different instructions. Families, employees and students should continue checking official HIDOE and agency communications because facility-specific conditions can change.

The reopening is a recovery milestone, but repair work continues across Kauaʻi. Essential services and emergency operations remained active during the closures, and state, county, utility and response crews are continuing work on power, roads and damaged infrastructure.

stories.headline: Oʻahu drivers face H-1, Nimitz and Farrington lane closures this week
stories.summary: HDOT lists overnight and daytime work from September 13–18, including H-1 closures near Kunia and Waipahu, Nimitz/Ala Moana construction and Farrington Highway utility work.
stories.why_it_matters: West and central Oʻahu commuters should allow extra time, especially during Sunday-through-Thursday night work and weekday construction windows.
body: Oʻahu motorists should plan for multiple state highway lane closures during the week of September 13–18, according to the Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation. Schedules may change without notice and all work is weather permitting.

On the H-1 Freeway near Kunia and Waipahu, HDOT lists two eastbound lanes closed between the Kunia Road on-ramp and the Fort Weaver Road/Kunia Road underpass from 8 p.m. to 4 a.m. Sunday through Tuesday nights for concrete replacement and precast panel work.

Additional weekday and nighttime work is listed along the H-1 corridor between Waipahu and ʻAiea. Drivers should watch posted signs and current HDOT notices because some listed closures serve as backup windows if weather changes the primary work schedule.

In urban Honolulu, daytime and nighttime construction affects parts of Nimitz Highway and Ala Moana Boulevard, including work near ʻIwilei, downtown and Ward Avenue. Some 24-hour HART-related lane restrictions also remain in place along the Nimitz corridor.

Farrington Highway work includes an eastbound lane closure near Ko Olina from 8 p.m. to 4 a.m. Sunday through Thursday nights for electrical trenching, along with other construction and traffic-control activity in ʻEwa Beach and Waipahu. Drivers should check the official weekly closure page immediately before travel.
